findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve how the push-path preflight fires without violating push_tickets_branch's best-effort (returns-None-on-failure / strict-only-raise) contract: state whether it raises unconditionally, respects `strict`, or gates only the synchronous-push arm.
evidence: push.py docstring: 'ALWAYS returns None (best-effort): a push failure never fails the caller'
push_tickets_branch(base_path, *, strict=False); failures go through _raise_if_strict which only raises when strict is True
AC-1 requires 'the push path' to 'exit non-zero' — incompatible with a swallowed best-effort failure
findings.finding: The push-path preflight collides with push_tickets_branch's best-effort contract: the function ALWAYS returns None on failure (raising only when strict=True), so a require_s3_helper() raise 'at the start' either breaks best-effort (crashes every ticket write on a misconfigured s3 remote) or is swallowed (no fail-closed, defeating the AC).
findings.location: Approach / Scope: 'add the preflight call at the top of push_tickets_branch' (src/rebar/_store/push.py)
scenarios: An auto-push (default strict=False) with an s3:// remote and a missing helper: the OptionalDependencyError either propagates and turns a best-effort write into a hard crash, or is caught and the guard silently does nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Place the guard inside the mode=='always' synchronous arm (right where the configured remote URL is already fetched at push.py:418), and make it raise regardless of `strict` (a misconfiguration is not a transient delivery failure) — or scope the story to init-only gating and justify why push transitively inherits it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the preflight handles a failed/absent remote URL resolution (no remote, get-url non-zero) — treat as non-S3 no-op vs. propagate — so the guard neither crashes nor is silently bypassed.
evidence: 'Resolve the configured remote's URL with git remote get-url <sync.remote>'
'When the remote URL is not s3:// (the default GitHub case) the preflight is a no-op'
findings.finding: The plan adds a new shell-out (git remote get-url) preflight on the hot push path and at init but does not specify behavior when the remote URL cannot be resolved — e.g. sync.remote is unset, the named remote does not exist, or git remote get-url exits non-zero. This new failure point could either crash unexpectedly or, worse, be swallowed and treated as non-S3 (bypassing the guard).
scenarios: sync.remote configured but the git remote is not yet added at push time → git remote get-url returns non-zero; unclear whether the preflight raises, aborts the push, or silently proceeds
No sync.remote configured at all → resolution failure with undefined handling
findings.suggested_fix: State that resolve_remote_url returning empty/error is treated as a non-S3 no-op (guard skipped, existing behavior preserved), since a missing/unresolvable remote cannot be an s3:// remote.
